rules.statement: The appellants must prove undue influence, and it is not sufficient to rely on suspicion alone.
rules.supporting_quote: "But, if in the progress of a testamentary case circumstances of suspicion arise, whether from the fact that the parties propounding a will benefit largely under its provisions and have been instrumental in securing its execution (Fulton v. Andrew (1) ; Parker v. Duncan v. Duncan (2) or otherwise for the rule has been held to be one of general application (Tyrrell v. Painton (3) ), the suspicion must be removed by the executors. They must satisfy the Court that the will is the act of a free, as well as a capable, testator."
